body.statement: Fix \(K=3\), \(T=5\), and the cohort--lag pair \((g,r)=(0,1)\). Along \(\mathfrak C_N\), both six-date realizations have strictly positive initial probabilities, transitions, emissions, interior hazards, and \(p_0>0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Their stopped-word probabilities agree exactly when \(\zeta_N=0\); at the declared \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), \(\operatorname{KL}(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})=O(\zeta_N^2)\) and \(\operatorname{KL}((P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N},(P_{W,N}^{(1)})^{\otimes N})=O(N\zeta_N^2)=O(N^{-1})\). Under \(P_{W,N}^{(0)}\), the declared canonical matrix with \(d=2\) satisfies \(\sigma_3(V_D)=(10.33271+o(1))\zeta_N\), while \((\mu^0_{0,1})^{(1)}-(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(0)}=63\eta_N/544+o(\eta_N)\); the common deterministic treated outcome gives the opposite gap for \(\tau_{0,1}\). Hence the product-law total variation tends to zero, the \(\tau_{0,1}\) separation is of order \(N^{-1/4}\), this path lies in \(0<\sigma_3(V_D)\le\rho_N\), and for every fixed \(\alpha_0<1/2\) no confidence band for \(\tau_{0,1}\) can have uniform \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage over this pair and diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) in probability under both product laws.
body.justification: This lower bound limits the proposal's own guarded fixed-chart hazard-lift plug-in on the displayed \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\) pair.
body.gap: Andrews and Cheng provide weak-identification precedent. The displayed path is a hazard-lift-specific modulus and does not contradict Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez or Callaway and Sant'Anna on their separated regular domains.
body.consumer: Analysts using this proposal's fixed-chart plug-in receive an explicit gray-zone rule: over the displayed pair, no band combines uniform \(1-\alpha_0\) coverage with \(o(N^{-1/4})\) diameter.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\eta=\eta_N\), \(\zeta=\zeta_N\), and \(S=S_{\star}\).  The first realization converges as \((\eta,\zeta)\to(0,0)\) to a model whose initial probabilities, transitions, emissions, hazards, and survival probabilities are all strictly positive.  For the second realization,
\[
 \alpha^{(1)}=\left(\frac{31}{100},\frac{39}{100},\frac3{10}\right),
 \qquad
 h^{(1)}=\left(\frac3{20}-\frac54\eta,\frac3{20}+\frac54\eta,\frac9{20}\right)^{\top}, \tag{28}
\]
and at \(\eta=0\),
\[
 P^{(1)}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 49/80&5/16&3/40\\
 3/16&39/80&13/40\\
 11/100&19/100&7/10
 \end{pmatrix}.                                                \tag{29}
\]
Every displayed entry in (28)--(29) is positive.  The formula defining \(P_N^{(1)}\) is continuous wherever the components of \(1-h_N^{(1)}\) are positive.  Hence all its entries, all hazards and survivals, and both binary emission probabilities are strictly positive for sufficiently large \(N\).  Directly,
\[
 p_0=\alpha_{\star}h_N^{(0)}=\frac{5\eta+12}{50}>0.            \tag{30}
\]
Stochasticity of \(P_N^{(1)}\) follows without an extra assumption: since \(S\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3\),
\[
 K_{0,N}^{(1)}\mathbf 1_3
 =S^{-1}(\mathbf 1_3-h_N^{(0)})
 =\mathbf 1_3-h_N^{(1)},
\]
so \(P_N^{(1)}\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3\).

When \(\zeta=0\), the first two emission probabilities coincide and therefore \(SB_a^{\star}=B_a^{\star}S\) for \(a=0,1\).  It follows exactly that
\[
 M_{a,N}^{(1)}=S^{-1}M_{a,N}^{(0)}S,
 \quad \alpha_N^{(1)}=\alpha_{\star}S,
 \quad h_N^{(1)}=S^{-1}h_N^{(0)},
 \quad S\mathbf 1_3=\mathbf 1_3.                              \tag{31}
\]
For every stopped word \(w\), multiplying (31) gives equality of both terminal series:
\[
 \alpha_N^{(1)}M_{w,N}^{(1)}\mathbf 1_3
 =\alpha_{\star}M_{w,N}^{(0)}\mathbf 1_3,
 \qquad
 \alpha_N^{(1)}M_{w,N}^{(1)}h_N^{(1)}
 =\alpha_{\star}M_{w,N}^{(0)}h_N^{(0)}.                       \tag{32}
\]
The treated-outcome law is common by construction, so the complete observed laws agree at \(\zeta=0\).

The support of a six-date stopped panel is finite.  On its common nonzero support, strict positivity at the limit supplies a cell-probability lower bound independent of sufficiently small \(\eta,\zeta\).  Every cell probability is a finite product and sum of entries of the displayed matrices and is therefore analytic near the limit.  Equation (32) says that the difference of corresponding cells vanishes at \(\zeta=0\), uniformly for small \(\eta\); hence
\[
 \max_x|p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)-q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)|=O(\zeta).       \tag{33}
\]
Using \(\log u\le u-1\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(p_{\eta,\zeta},q_{\eta,\zeta})
 \le\sum_x\frac{\{p_{\eta,\zeta}(x)-q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)\}^2}{q_{\eta,\zeta}(x)}
 =O(\zeta^2).                                                  \tag{34}
\]
Expansion of the product log likelihood gives additivity of relative entropy, so at \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left((P_{W,N}^{(0)})^{\otimes N},(P_{W,N}^{(1)})^{\otimes N}\right)
 =N\operatorname{KL}(P_{W,N}^{(0)},P_{W,N}^{(1)})=O(N^{-1}).   \tag{35}
\]
Alternatively, the chi-square quantity on the right of (34) is \(O(\zeta^2)\), and
\[
 1+\chi^2(p^{\otimes N},q^{\otimes N})=\{1+\chi^2(p,q)\}^{N}.
\]
Thus the product chi-square divergence is \(O(N^{-1})\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|p^{\otimes N}-q^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(p^{\otimes N},q^{\otimes N})}=O(N^{-1/2})\to0. \tag{36}
\]

We next reproduce the declared singular-value constant.  At \(\eta=\zeta=0\), direct rational multiplication for the corrected chart gives
\[
 H=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1&6/25&2847/25000\\
 509/1000&2847/25000&1506459/25000000\\
 251/1000&3651/50000&601221/25000000
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det H=\frac{257499}{31250000000}\ne0.                       \tag{37}
\]
For this chart let
\[
 C(\eta,\zeta)=\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf 1_3&h_N^{(0)}&B_{0,N}^{\star}K_{0,N}^{(0)}h_N^{(0)}\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The realization factorization proved for the finite chart implies
\[
 V_D(\eta,\zeta)
 =C(\eta,\zeta)^{-1}
 \begin{bmatrix}\mathbf 1_3&B_{1,N}^{\star}\mathbf 1_3&(B_{1,N}^{\star})^2\mathbf 1_3\end{bmatrix}. \tag{38}
\]
At \(\eta=0\), exact simplification of (38) yields
\[
 V_D(0,0)=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1/10&-13/50\\0&2&2\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det V_D(0,\zeta)=-\frac{500\zeta(5\zeta-3)}{51(5\zeta-1)}. \tag{39}
\]
The product of the two nonzero singular values of \(V_D(0,0)\) is the square root of the sum of squares of its two-by-two minors, namely
\[
 \sigma_1\{V_D(0,0)\}\sigma_2\{V_D(0,0)\}=\frac{2\sqrt{1266}}{25}. \tag{40}
\]
Since the product of all three singular values is the absolute determinant, (39)--(40), continuity, and \(\eta_N\to0\) imply
\[
 \sigma_3\{V_D(\eta_N,\zeta_N)\}
 =\left(\frac{6250}{17\sqrt{1266}}+o(1)\right)\zeta_N
 =\{10.332710061\ldots+o(1)\}\zeta_N.                         \tag{41}
\]
Indeed, at \(\zeta=0\) the first two latent entries of each of \(\mathbf 1_3\), \(B_{1,N}^{\star}\mathbf 1_3\), and \((B_{1,N}^{\star})^2\mathbf 1_3\) agree, so (38) has rank exactly two for every sufficiently small \(\eta\).  Thus there is no term depending only on \(\eta\); the first-order coefficient in \(\zeta\) is continuous at \(\eta=0\), which justifies evaluating it through (39)--(40) along \(\eta_N\to0\).
In particular this singular value is positive for large \(N\), and
\[
 \frac{\sigma_3(V_D)}{\rho_N}
 =O\!\left(\frac{N^{-1}}{\sqrt{\log N/N}}\right)\to0.         \tag{42}
\]
Thus the displayed population moment lies in the sampling-noise component \(0<\sigma_3(V_D)\le\rho_N\) of the gray zone.

Finally, direct substitution in the two latent causal means gives the exact difference
\[
 \Delta(\eta,\zeta)
 :=(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(1)}-(\mu^0_{0,1})^{(0)}
 =-\frac{3\{87500\eta^3\zeta+18000\eta^2\zeta+9000\eta^2+22015\eta\zeta+53550\eta-3468\zeta\}}
 {400(5\eta+12)(25\eta-17)(25\eta+17)}.                      \tag{43}
\]
All denominators in (43) are nonzero for sufficiently small positive \(\eta\).  Since \(\zeta_N=\eta_N^4\), expansion at zero yields
\[
 \Delta(\eta_N,\zeta_N)=\frac{63}{544}\eta_N+o(\eta_N).      \tag{44}
\]
The treated outcome is the same deterministic constant in both laws, so the ATT difference is \(-\Delta\).

To prove the final impossibility statement, let \(C_N\) be any confidence band with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0\) under both product laws, and write their two ATT values as \(\theta_{0,N}\) and \(\theta_{1,N}\).  By (36), under the first product law,
\[
 \Pr(\theta_{0,N}\in C_N)\ge1-\alpha_0-o(1),
 \qquad
 \Pr(\theta_{1,N}\in C_N)\ge1-\alpha_0-o(1).
\]
The union bound therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\bigl(\theta_{0,N},\theta_{1,N}\in C_N\bigr)
 \ge1-2\alpha_0-o(1)>0.                                      \tag{45}
\]
On the event in (45), \(\operatorname{diam}(C_N)\ge|\theta_{1,N}-\theta_{0,N}|=(63/544+o(1))N^{-1/4}\), contradicting diameter \(o(N^{-1/4})\) in probability.  This completes every assertion of the proposition.
